title: Jurassic Park
summary: Blockbuster sci-fi monster film based on Michael Crichton's novel, pioneering photorealistic CGI dinosaur animation created by Industrial Light & Magic (ILM).
facts: Directed by Steven Spielberg with practical animatronics designed by Stan Winston.
ILM CGI animation led by Dennis Muren revolutionized computer graphics in Hollywood.
Became the highest-grossing film of all time upon release, earning over $914 million worldwide.

title: The Matrix
summary: Cyberpunk sci-fi masterpiece starring Keanu Reeves as Neo, famous for introducing 'Bullet Time' visual effects, wire-fu action, and simulation theory.
facts: Directed by Lana and Lilly Wachowski.
Bullet time effect achieved using custom arrays of green-screen still cameras triggered sequentially.
Won 4 Academy Awards including Best Visual Effects and Best Sound.

title: Pulp Fiction
summary: Non-linear neo-noir crime masterpiece written and directed by Quentin Tarantino, redefining independent cinema and pop-culture dialogue.
facts: Won the Palme d'Or at the 1994 Cannes Film Festival and Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay.
Revitalized John Travolta's acting career alongside iconic roles for Samuel L. Jackson and Uma Thurman.
First indie film to surpass $100 million at the US box office.

title: Titanic
manufacturer: Paramount Pictures / 20th Century Fox / James Cameron
summary: Epic romantic disaster film directed by James Cameron starring Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet, becoming the highest-grossing film of the 20th century.
facts: Tied the record for most Academy Award wins (11 Oscars) including Best Picture and Best Director.
First film to cross the $1 billion box office threshold worldwide.
Soundtrack featuring Celine Dion's 'My Heart Will Go On' sold over 30 million copies.

title: Toy Story
manufacturer: Pixar Animation Studios / Walt Disney Pictures
summary: The world's first fully computer-animated feature film, directed by John Lasseter and featuring the voices of Tom Hanks (Woody) and Tim Allen (Buzz Lightyear).
facts: Produced at Pixar using RenderMan software on Silicon Graphics (SGI) workstations.
Earned a Special Achievement Academy Award for director John Lasseter.
Grossed over $373 million and launched Pixar as a premier feature film studio.
